Why you’re seeing this example

How GitHub would power this — for free

Everything above is one simple website. On GitHub, it would live in one place, cost $0 to host, and every change would be saved like a version history for your files.

🌐 GitHub Pages = this site, live

Push this page to a repo like graycodeentertainment.github.io and it’s online free. Add your own domain later if you want — e.g. graycodeent.com.

🗂️ Versions, not v1 v2 v3 v4

Instead of Folded-promo-v4.mp4, cover-final-FINAL.jpg everywhere, GitHub tracks what changed, when, and lets you roll back.

👥 One shared home

EPKs, pitch drafts, lyrics, tracklists, and this site in one repo the team can see — instead of scattered across email and drives.

What GitHub is NOT good for

Big WAV masters and video files don’t belong in GitHub — file limits make it painful. Keep masters in Drive / Dropbox, and keep only the site, documents, and small assets in GitHub.

What it would cost

$0 for a public Pages site. A custom domain is the only optional cost (usually ~$10–15/year from a registrar) — GitHub hosting itself stays free.

Next step if you like this look

Say the word and we set up a GCE GitHub organization, drop this design in as the real site, and replace the example photos with real HoodBoss / Cam Webbe photos and covers.
